clue.text: Writer's side cured

definitions.meaning: Francis ..., the Elizabethan essayist and philosopher
a cured side of pork, sliced into rashers

explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was an English essayist, and a salted, smoked flank of pig is the breakfast meat of the same name.

clue.text: Prohibit Church taking a shaky loan in Spain

parts.note: to prohibit is to bar
CE stands for the Church of England

indicators.note: a shaky loan is unsteady, so its letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A church borrows money on wobbly terms from a Spanish bank and is promptly banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaky' is the anagram signal for 'loan'; 'taking a' only joins. The definition 'in Spain' is a place found there, the Catalan capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalonia's capital is a major city on Spain's Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Creeper needs firm support

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a bra is an item of supporting underwear

explanation.surface: A climbing plant needs something sturdy to hold it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creeper' suggests a climbing plant, but here it is a snake that creeps along the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake slithers along the ground, so a hooded venomous serpent is a creeper.

clue.text: Upset Una, tease and sicken her

indicators.note: to upset things is to knock them into disorder, so the letters of the two names are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone teases a woman called Una until she feels ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' rearranges UNA plus TEASE; 'her' completes the picture of Una being made ill.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone feel queasy and ready to vomit is to sicken them.

clue.text: Savage makes Cuttle run

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are made into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fierce character forces Captain Cuttle, from Dickens's Dombey and Son, to flee.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Cuttle is a character in Dickens's Dombey and Son. 'makes' tells you to make a new word from the letters of CUTTLE and RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fierce and aggressively defiant is described as savage in temper.

clue.text: Time the Movement in C is heard

definitions.meaning: an old word for a season or time, as in Eastertide

definitions.text: the Movement in C is heard
definitions.meaning: C said out loud is 'sea', and the regular rise and fall of the sea is its movement

explanation.definitionFit: The word survives as 'time' in Yuletide, and it is also the ocean's twice-daily ebb and flow.

clue.text: One the foreigners run in burlesque, but make a slip

parts.note: un is French for one
der is German for the; 'foreigners' tells you both words are foreign

indicators.note: the run goes inside the burlesque

parts.note: a skit is a comic parody or burlesque
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Foreign performers stage a comic show but someone makes a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside SKIT to make SKIRT. 'slip' looks like an error, but it is a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a woman's light garment worn beneath a dress or skirt.

clue.text: Nudity, curiously out of place

indicators.note: curiously suggests something done in an odd way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Being naked here would seem oddly inappropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' rearranges NUDITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are out of place make a room messy and disordered.

clue.text: Elevating East German capital to rise above the heath

indicators.note: in a down entry the first part sits above the next

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for East

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word Bonn is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Bonn was the capital of West Germany
ling is heather, the plant of the heath

explanation.surface: A West German capital is raised up over open moorland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rise' turns BONN into NNOB in this down clue; 'above' places it over LING. Bonn was West Germany's capital until 1990.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising someone to the peerage, making them a noble, is elevating them.

clue.text: Bird with the French name

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A bird is given a French name.
explanation.definitionFit: A book or person's title is the name by which it is known.

clue.text: Recoiled, though not necessarily from marriage

definitions.text: Recoiled, though not necessarily from marriage

parts.words: Recoiled, though not necessarily from marriage
parts.note: bounced back, with a nod to someone who has split up and is 'on the rebound'

explanation.definitionFit: Something that sprang back after hitting a surface did so, like a ball bouncing off a wall.

clue.text: In wine there is a point of principle

indicators.note: the point goes inside the word for wine

parts.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine
E is East, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Wine drinking holds a point of principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts E inside TENT, a red wine from Spain; 'there is' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrine or belief held as true is a principle.

clue.text: Reactionary story by journalist in high spirits

indicators.note: something reactionary goes backwards, so the word for story is read in reverse

parts.note: a tale is a story
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist with right-wing views files a cheerful story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reactionary' signals the reversal: a reactionary wants to turn the clock back.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thrilled and joyful is in high spirits.

clue.text: Convincing cheese replacement, initially fit to eat

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: food fit to eat is edible

explanation.surface: A substitute cheese that is actually fit to eat is persuasive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' covers both 'cheese' and 'replacement', giving C and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A believable, plausible argument is convincing.

clue.text: Beefy team which came in second?

definitions.text: Beefy team which came in second?

parts.words: Beefy team which came in second?
parts.note: a joint of beef, read as a side (team) that took the silver medal for coming second

explanation.definitionFit: It is a cut of beef from the hindquarter, and the name splits into a runner-up's medal colour plus a team.

clue.text: Patent stacks — more than one bargained for

parts.note: patent means obvious or overt
ricks are haystacks

explanation.surface: Obvious piles of hay turn out to be more than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, tricks won beyond the contract bid are this; 'bargained for' is the bid.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, tricks taken above the number contracted are extra to the bargain struck in the bidding.

clue.text: More mixed diet to send home

parts.note: extra means more

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bigger, more varied diet is sent home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' signals the anagram of 'diet'; 'to send home' is the definition as a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand a fugitive over to their home country for trial is to send them back.

clue.text: Complain vociferously to some about drink

indicators.note: for some speakers, who do not sound the h, the word for complaining is heard identically

parts.note: to whine is to complain loudly

explanation.surface: Someone complains loudly to a group about their drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone works only 'to some', those who say WH like plain W.
explanation.definitionFit: Fermented grape juice is a drink.

clue.text: Sent to the fourth gate

parts.note: a gate is an entrance
D is the fourth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone was dispatched to Gate 4.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent' looks like dispatched, but it means delighted, carried away; read gate D, the fourth gate.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sent, in the old slang of rapture, is enthralled and spellbound.

clue.text: Mad when called during the act

indicators.note: the call goes during, inside, the act

parts.note: a deed is an act
rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: Someone was furious when phoned in the middle of the act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' is the container signal: the call happens in the middle of the act; 'when' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone insane or deranged is mad.

clue.text: Book for performances

definitions.meaning: the ... of the Apostles, a book of the New Testament

explanation.definitionFit: The Acts of the Apostles is a New Testament book, and turns on a variety bill are stage performances.

clue.text: More to attend, say, not having dieted

parts.note: over means more than

indicators.note: say means the word for attending is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to wait on someone is to attend them

explanation.surface: Someone has more to wait for because they did not stick to their diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns WAIT into its sound-alike WEIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone too heavy has plainly not been slimming.

clue.text: Looks hard at floating vetch

annotationWithheld.why: Looks hard at floating vetch (6): vetch is TARES (or ERS) but no word gives the leading S, and 'floating' signals nothing that makes STARES; the scan prints the same words, so a word looks lost or misprinted

clue.text: Break wrecked craft by the river

indicators.note: a wrecked craft is smashed up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A boat is smashed to pieces beside the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' rearranges CRAFT to FRACT; the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracture is a crack or break, as in a bone.

clue.text: I'll — and be perverse" (R and J)

definitions.text: I'll — and be perverse" (R and J)

parts.words: I'll — and be perverse" (R and J)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Romeo and Juliet, where Juliet says she will scowl, be contrary and say Romeo nay

explanation.definitionFit: Juliet's line runs that she would scowl and be perverse and say thee nay, the missing word meaning to look displeased.

clue.text: Venue for wedding without notice in N America

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the wedding venue goes round the notice

parts.note: Cana in Galilee, where Jesus turned water into wine at a wedding
an ad is a notice

explanation.surface: Someone marries suddenly somewhere in North America without telling anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, its old sense, not lacking; Cana is the Galilee village of the wedding at which water became wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The country lies in the north of the continent, north of the United States.

clue.text: Musical strip girl …

definitions.meaning: a Broadway show about an orphan girl
Little Orphan ..., the American comic strip heroine

explanation.definitionFit: The musical about an orphan was based on Little Orphan Annie, a comic-strip girl.

clue.text: … and this, etc, before long

parts.note: so means this much, as in 'about so high' said with a gesture
etc stands for continuing a list, carrying on, which on expresses as in 'and so forth and on'

explanation.surface: Continuing a list of things that will come shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on from 24, and 'and' joins; the pieces echo the phrase that etc abbreviates.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortly, presently, in a little while: all mean before long.

clue.text: Outfitter loses his head in the plant

indicators.note: the outfitter loses his first letter

parts.note: a hosier sells stockings and other clothing

explanation.surface: A tailor is beheaded among the shrubbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses his head' drops the H from HOSIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A willow whose pliant shoots are used in basketry is a plant.

clue.text: In wind pipes, most of the ice is artificial

parts.note: taken as written
an organ is an instrument of wind-blown pipes

indicators.note: most of a word means it loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Ice forms in wind instruments and looks fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' leaves IC from ICE; 'the' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Not derived from living matter, so synthetic or man-made.

clue.text: Detailed interest in trip in Germany

indicators.note: trip suggests stumbling, so the letters fall into a new order
de-tailed means having its tail, the last letter, removed

explanation.surface: A detailed interest in a trip to Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' cuts the final T from INTEREST, leaving INTERES; 'trip' rearranges that with IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rhine town and the white wine named after it are found in Germany.

clue.text: Fear of father when billeting soldiers

indicators.note: billeting means housing soldiers, so the father takes the soldiers in

parts.note: dad is father
RE stands for the Royal Engineers, soldiers

explanation.surface: Father fears soldiers being quartered in his house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when billeting' is the container signal: billeted soldiers are lodged inside a household; 'of' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear or terror.
